Only some situations count: those in which the condition of the requirement is the case (what comes after WHEN, WHILE or IF; a requirement without such a part has no condition, and every situation counts), and in which the system has done everything the requirement demands, with its words read exactly as written. A situation in which the condition is not the case does not count, although the requirement is not broken in it. Must B be true in every situation that counts? Answer:

This is also the answer when B would usually come before what the requirement demands, or when a system would need B to bring it about. Do not assume how the system works, or that anything succeeds (if it demands that the gate is open, nobody need have opened it today; if it demands that the bell is rung once, the bell need not have been heard).
- unclear: the words can reasonably be read both ways.
